To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) learning from examples can be viewed as an inverse problem; (2) the probabilistic analysis of inverse problems can be used to obtain consistency bounds in learning theory; (3) the stability of the solution is an important property for learning from examples; (4) the consistency of learning from examples is closely related to the stability of the inverse problem.

(1) the probabilistic bound for regularization algorithms in the continuous case is a natural extension of the discrete case and (2) the consistency of the regularized least squares algorithm can be easily derived by using the probabilistic bound and standard approximation results.
the consistency approach imposed by learning theory can be viewed as a stability convergence property, and that the regularized least squares algorithm is a consistent learning method.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the consistency of the learning algorithm is equivalent to the stability of the inverse problem.
the consistency of a learning algorithm is a consequence of the stability convergence of the inverse problem.

the consistency of the regularized least-square algorithm in the continuous (population, or infinite sample size) case is a consequence of two facts: 1) the stability of the inverse problem and 2) the approximation of the true solution of the inverse problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the regularization approach to learning from examples can be viewed as a generalization of the consistency approach to learning.
we provide a new probabilistic interpretation for regularization methods and we establish the connection between learning theory and inverse problems in a natural way.
we have established the connection between the two main approaches in the field of learning from examples: the consistency approach and the stability approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the probabilistic analysis of the regularized algorithm can be carried out in a unified framework for both the continuous and the discrete problems, and that the probabilistic bounds are essentially equivalent to those obtained by using the stability approach.
the probabilistic analysis of the regularization algorithms is a very useful tool for the analysis of the consistency of learning algorithms.

the probabilistic analysis of learning algorithms can provide a new insight into the stability properties of inverse problems and, vice versa, that the analysis of inverse problems can provide a new tool for the analysis of learning algorithms.
